final_assessment: Redesign session after the first fresh proposal pass returned 5 CRITICAL. Triaged under R-crc-6's lanes and ratified: three repairs, one redesign, no return to propose-from-scratch. The redesign is D-rc03a-7, which REVERSES D-rc03a-3: the rule now keys on a CONJUNCTION (slot == blind-pair AND the invoked reviewer class is independent) and fires only on a positive signal, with no fail-closed branch. The single-key rule failed two ways at once because `next_hint_keys.slot` answers what the engine recommends NEXT rather than what the pass in hand IS — it withheld from sequential iterations whenever the slot was absent (the routine state between a review and its walk) and blinded in-context passes during the pair window. Fail-closed was reversed rather than defended because it was argued on a consequence asymmetry that only holds if it misfires rarely, and it misfires on two routine states. Case 1's table was corrected: two slot values were wrong and, more importantly, the two absent-slot rows were missing entirely — their absence is precisely what let fail-closed ship as if undeterminable slots were rare. A table can be wrong in a cell and right in its conclusion; only the omitted rows mattered. Also recorded: /orbit:explore has no defined behavior for a name that already promoted, so this session resumed in place by judgment with nothing in the body sanctioning it.
